newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares could consolidate further.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares could consolidate further.

text.p: A weaker performance on Wall Street in the afternoon brought renewed pressure to bear on Brussels along with its neighbours, with opinion divided over how much longer the current consolidation period would go on.

"It is a conflicting market at historic levels -- rates have never been better, but some people are worried they have reached the bottom," one dealer said, adding he believed there was room for rates to go lower still.
The Bel-20 index .BFX closed 8.30 points or 0.47 percent lower at 1,769.75, with overall Belgian share market volume worth a moderate 1.9 billion francs.
Discounter Colruyt continued to outperform fellow retailers, closing 1.6 percent up at 13,000.

Steel-maker Arbed, which said late Tuesday it made a small group loss in first half 1996 after a large profit in the year ago period, ended 1.5 percent lower at 3,700. The results were at the bottom end of the range of expectations.
Analysts said Arbed stock still looked cheap versus others in the sector and had potential to rally in the long term.
One dealer said Generale Bank continued to suffer from its one-for-10 capital increase, and the stock finished 50 francs down at 10,725.
